details.detail: Sidewall panels and seams. Smooth satin off-white. A seam sits mid-pier after every second window (Y pier 0.123 m), matching y_47303 and sp_py_13. The studio wall renders #e6e5e3. The upper wall in assembled views is still washed blue, which belongs to LIGHTING (already reported). No stucco, no seam artefacts.

PY/Y window tub (REC_Y), PARTLY FIXED from w1 high. The tub now runs from v 0.66 to 1.585, just under the bins at 1.60. It is 0.41 m wide (0.77 of the pitch against about 0.80 in the photos) with a 0.25 m lower bowl. That matches the photo lower bowl of about 0.24 m (y_47303, py_37301). The opening is still centred vertically in the tub (0.23 m above, 0.25 m below). In y_47303, f_17313 and sp_py_13 the opening sits in the lower part of the tub, with about 1.0-1.1 opening heights of tub above it at head-on views. This depends on the pane-centre height (see questions).

F/J recess (REC). It is 0.39 m wide, 0.1975 m of tub above the 0.445 m opening and 0.11 m below. The f_17313 window at x 170 measures recess y 80-365 against a bezel of y 170-335, so about 0.24 m above and 0.08 m below. Room-24 gives a sill of about 0.30 of the opening width (about 0.09 m) with the pill button in it. Close enough. The upper recess face (ext 12 mm) renders #e1e0dd against the wall's #e6e5e3 (0.98). The photos show 0.74-0.82, so the upper tub still reads nearly flat.

Recess lip tessellation. The 48-point ring gives only about 4-5 segments per 0.15 m top corner. The soft lip shows visible polygon kinks at the top corners in close views. There is also a lighter triangular shading wedge on the rolled opening lip at its upper-right corner.

F/J electric shades and blue-LED button: largely FIXED. There are 31 hemmed pleats of about 14 mm, matching the Room-24 FFT. The split pill has its blue ring and pinhole on the sill. Blackout against bezel renders 185/230 = 0.80 (studio). The photo is 0.62 (Room-24: shade #787367, bezel #c2baaa), up from 0.87 in w1. The sheer still shows serrated pleat ends along its side at oblique angles (s05 left window). Real pleated shades show a little of this too (Room-24 left edge), so it is only minor. At oblique distance the blackout pleats beat against the pixel grid: the win_oblique column profile flips phase every 10-12 px.

PY/Y manual shade: FIXED. The stowed shade shows a cream band about 36 mm deep plus a darker finger scoop under the top of the opening, which matches sp_py_24. The half and closed states read correctly (win_front, s08).

Dado and air-return grilles: PARTLY FIXED. The squarer grilles now nearly fill the facet (proportion OK), and the placard sits mid-pier as in py_37303. Three things are still off against the py_37303 close crop. (1) In the photo the grille is a cut-out in the dark dado panel, with the panel itself as its border. The render gives it a raised, lighter frame (#7d8595) that outlines every grille. (2) The photo grille reads as horizontal louvres with only 2-3 faint ribs. The render still shows 7 distinct vertical ribs. (3) The render grille field is too dark relative to the dado: render grille #232832 (lum 40) against dado #2f374d (lum 55), a ratio of 0.73. In the photos the grille is close to the panel tone (py_37301 grille #464d61, and py_37303 grille and panel nearly equal). The in-cabin dado is still bluer than the photos: saturation 0.39 against about 0.27.

Carpets and track covers. Y aisle #374361 against the photo's #2b325b-#36445f: OK. Door-area vinyl #64646c against sans_09's #666268: FIXED. F carpet is now brown #33271f (q02). The photo is greyer and a little lighter, #463a3a (f_17300) and #423838, so it has gone a little too dark and too brown.

Type A door surround and viewing window: PARTLY FIXED. The viewing window is now small and high (0.19 x 0.25 m at 1.52 m), and the seams are light. Two problems remain. The upper 22 % of the window hole is covered by a blue-lit surface. The hole is also a paper-thin cut-out with no tunnel, bezel or glass: the exterior shows straight through the wall. The door lining furniture (in 10_mono) is unchanged. The slide bustle is still gRBox(0.10, 0.36, 0.92) at v 0.30, and the red flag is still at v 1.62.

Window light on the wall and sun patches: owned by LIGHTING. The hard-edged pale rectangles round open windows are still present (s05 x 380-830, s08 x 330-560). The sun patches on the seats are still thin diagonal streaks (q14, s01).

issues.detail: The door viewing window is partly blocked and has no reveal or glass
issues.problem: The top 55 mm of the 1.395-1.645 m door window hole shows a flat blue-lit surface, which gives the window a flat top (s06 crop). buildShell's 'upper sidewall above the bin line' gSweep also runs through DOOR zones from WALL.vTop - 0.01 = 1.59 m to 2.02 m, 2 mm outboard of the door surround. That surround (windowCell with topRows [1.76, 1.80, 2.02]) already covers this height. The sweep therefore sits behind the hole, and it duplicates the surround 2 mm behind it, which risks z-fighting. The hole itself is a paper-thin cut: no tunnel, no bezel, no glass. The wing and sky are seen straight through the lining.
issues.evidence: r3/s06_door2 and r3/s07_door4, crops at (420-520, 200-290): the top ~22 % of the opening is a flat blue band with a straight lower edge. (1.645 - 1.59) / 0.25 = 22 %. No lining depth is visible at any edge.
issues.fix: src/07_shell.js buildShell, the upper-sidewall loop: change `if (zn.type === 'seat') continue;` to `if (zn.type === 'seat' || zn.type === 'door') continue;`. The door surround already reaches 2.02. In the door-surround loop, after windowCell(g, side, c, dp, topRows), add a short tunnel and a pane. const dmap = (dz, dv, d) => { const [x, y, nx, ny] = wallAt(1.52 + dv); return [(x - nx * d) * side, y - ny * d, c + dz]; }; const hr = dp.ring.map((p) => p.h); shell.add(ringLoft([[hr, 0], [hr.map(([a, b]) => [a * 0.96, b * 0.96]), 0.012], [hr.map(([a, b]) => [a * 0.88, b * 0.9]), 0.09]], dmap, [wallAt(1.52)[2] * side, wallAt(1.52)[3], 0]), null, WMAT.lining). Also add a glass disc at d = 0.09 (the same fan as windowParts' gl_) to a 'glassDoor' mesh drawn by the glass program, with castShadow false, as glassR / glassL are.

issues.detail: The dado grille has a raised light frame and prominent ribs; the photo shows a cut-out louvre field
issues.problem: In ANA's PY/Y cabin the air-return grille is an opening in the dark dado panel. The panel face is the border, and inside it are horizontal louvres with 2-3 faint ribs. The render adds a proud frame lighter than the dado that outlines each grille, and shows 7 clear ribs. The louvre field averages darker than the photo.
issues.evidence: py_37303 crop (190-350, 230-330): no light frame; grille and panel of almost equal tone; about 20 louvres; ribs barely visible. py_37301 grille #464d61. r3/s04 crop (640-900, 170-360): light frame ring, 7 ribs, grille #232832 against dado #2f374d (0.73).
issues.fix: src/07_shell.js WMAT: grilleFrame '#7d8595' -> '#5d6472' (at or below the dado, reading as the shadowed step into the panel), grilleBack '#30353f' -> '#3a404b', rib '#5a606d' -> '#3f4550'. windowParts: the frame loft [.., 0.0004], [.., 0.0064], [.., 0.0012] -> [.., 0.0004], [.., 0.0022], [.., 0.0010] so it is a low lip and not a bezel. Ribs: for k < 7 / k / 6 -> for k < 3 / lerp(-ghw + 0.08, ghw - 0.08, k / 2). The louvre count nSl 32 is fine.

issues.detail: The recess lip is faceted at the top corners, and there is a shading wedge on the rolled opening lip
issues.problem: windowCellPattern samples the recess outline with NR = 48 points by arc length, so each 0.15 m top-corner arc gets only about 4-5 segments. The soft 16 mm quarter-round lip shows the kinks. The sill loft ([inset(rr, 0.019), D] -> [scl(open, 1.085), D]) connects rings of very different lengths through the same angles, including the four cellular corner angles. That makes long, skinny triangles whose smoothed normals print a lighter triangular wedge at the opening's upper-right corner.
issues.evidence: r3/win_close crop (120-360, 20-200) at 3x: clear polygon kinks on both upper corners of the recess lip, and a lighter wedge at the opening's upper-right.
issues.fix: src/07_shell.js windowCellPattern: NR = 48 -> 96 (the wall hole, lip and sill share the ring, so they stay watertight). In windowParts, give the sill loft two intermediate rings, ringLoft([[inset(rr, 0.019), D, mapE], [lerp-ring(inset(rr, 0.019), scl(open, 1.085), 0.33), D], [lerp-ring(.., 0.66), D], [scl(open, 1.085), D]], ...). Then overwrite that part's normals with the wall normal at each vertex, as the lip's ring 0 does: n = [wallAt(vc + dv)[2] * side, wallAt(vc + dv)[3], 0]. The sill is near-planar, so smoothed normals only add wedges.

issues.detail: The opening sits centred in the PY/Y tub; photos show it in the lower part
issues.problem: The tub now reaches the bin line and has the right lower bowl. The opening, though, has 0.23 m of tub above and 0.25 m below. In the photos the tub above the opening is clearly taller than below.
issues.evidence: y_47303 x = 500 luminance profile: recess top edge y ~15, bright opening ~y 95-175, recess bottom hidden by seats but above y 215. So about 80 px above against 40 or fewer below. f_17313: 90 px above, 30 px below.
issues.fix: Only fixable with a height change: either lower CAB.win.yc from 1.13 to about 1.06 (05_layout shared; REC_Y.top 0.455 -> 0.525, bot -0.47 -> -0.40, so it stays 0.66-1.585), or raise the bin line (ceiling/bins owner). Needs the user's answer on whether 1.13 is sourced (see questions).

issues.detail: Blackout pleats alias into moiré at oblique distance
issues.problem: The baked valley/crest stripe alternates every row. At oblique angles the pleat period nears 2-3 px and beats.
issues.evidence: r3/win_oblique column x = 100, y 230-330: the alternating pattern flips phase every 10-12 px (for example 206, 199, 190, 178, 203).
issues.fix: src/07_shell.js shadePanelGeo: bake the stripe as a soft two-row ramp (valley x kf, crest rows x 1, and the hem columns c = 0 and 3 x (1 + kf) / 2). Alternatively cut kf to 0.80 for the blackout and raise the zig-zag zz 0.005 -> 0.006, so geometric shading (which the MSAA resolves) carries more of the stripe than the vertex colour does.
